evidence: Type census of the frozen task (grep '^type' across all five judge.toml): 50 binary, 5 likert; criterion counts render 1, constraints 1, functional 43, polish 5, visual 5. (1) Gates: hro_gate_render (gates/render/judge.toml:17-24) and hro_gate_shared (gates/constraints/judge.toml:17-24) are type = "binary" under aggregation = "all_pass", matching staged-task-contract.md:96 'their criteria stay binary'. (2) Functional: all 43 criteria are binary pass/fail behaviours with explicit 'Fails if ...' conditions and controls (e.g. hro_interview_full functional/judge.toml:104-111 'moving another single card into Interview is refused by the server ... Fails if the single-card move ... is accepted'); none describe a degree of quality. Gradation comes from per-criterion weights 0.5-2.5 under weighted_mean, consistent with the internal annotation's 'binary and weighted' practice. (3) Polish: 5 binary criteria (polish/judge.toml:17-60), each an objectively observable preservation behaviour (draft text exact, document.activeElement, scroll offset unchanged, getBoundingClientRect().top within a few pixels, sent once). These are pass/fail behaviours, not craft judgements, so binary fits; this mirrors the template polish dimension, which is also all binary. (4) Visual: 5 craft criteria hro_vis_type/color/layout/hierarchy/consistency (visual/judge.toml:17-90), each type = "likert", points = 5, with a described anchor at every level 5,4,3,2,1 (e.g. lines 24-29: '5: clear consistent type scale ... 1: typography broadly illegible or unstructured.'). No craft criterion is binary (no lost gradation) and no likert block is missing anchors — the two failure modes SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170 say to flag. Presence of likert is not flagged per the documented known false positive, despite the internal note 'Likert we dont use in rewrdkit'. Prompts are consistent with the types: visual/prompt.md:7 and :12 say lowest is 'Likert 1', 'minimum raw Likert score 1, which normalizes to zero'; polish/prompt.md:12/18 use binary0. Probes: (a) broken app that could pass — a visually polished but behaviourally dead app: the binary gates (independent-context readback) zero it, and visual likert is not reached; a partially-correct app cannot gain partial credit on a single binary functional row, but this is the intended pass/fail semantics with gradation across 43 weighted rows. (b) conforming alternative that could fail — an unconventional but deliberate visual design is graded by descriptive anchors rather than a hidden binary style rule, so it is not forced to 0. No defect found for this row. Non-blocking observation (not a row-41 defect, recorded for owners): the template visual anchors run 0-5 while the task's run 1-5 with the prompt asserting raw 1 normalizes to 0; the actual RewardKit likert normalization for points=5 was not measured by any configured judge run (raw-evidence-index scope says none exists). This affects reward magnitude (rows 40/42), not whether types fit the ask.
